name: Laws of the East

sources: Mind's Eye Theatre: Laws of the East (WW05016), "Weapon Examples"/Armor chapter, pp.186-191 - every entry checked against the accumulated catalog so far (Dark Epics, Laws of the Night Revised Edition, Laws of the Hunt); a same-name entry whose stats match an already-catalogued one is left out of this file.
Every entry read directly from the book's own page images (not OCR), per reference-wod-scan-ocr-lessons. This copy's own printed page numbers are plain, legible Arabic numerals.

notes: A Kuei-Jin/Cathaya-themed sourcebook, so most of its own weapon content is genuinely new rather than a reprint - 10 of its 20-odd printed entries carry real stats, far more than Laws of the Hunt's own 2.

Staff/Spear prints one stat block covering two different weapons at once ("Damage: Staff - 2 health levels; Spear - 3 health levels", one shared Bonus/Negative/Concealability/Availability) - split here into two ordinary entries, the same reasoning as Club/Ax in the other two MET corebooks already catalogued.
Katana's own text explicitly states "Negative Traits: None" - kept as a real, deliberate empty list, not an omitted field.
Shuriken prints no Availability line at all on this page, unlike every other entry in this chapter - left unset here rather than invented.

items.name: Shuriken
items.description: A character must possess either Melee or Martial Arts to throw shuriken; Athletics alone is not enough, though Athletics may be used to throw them if the other requirements are met. Spray: a character with at least one level in both Melee or Martial Arts and Athletics may throw up to half their permanent Melee/Martial Arts level (round up) in one attack.

items.name: Sash

availability.name: Almost any clothing store, though most Kuei-jin prefer sashes of fairly high quality, if only for aesthetic purposes

items.description: A weapon unique to the East. Melee alone is not enough - appropriate Martial Arts training lets skilled practitioners entangle and blind their foes, and true masters can even whip the sash with sufficient force and precision to slash their foes as if it were metal.

items.name: Nunchaku
items.description: Covers the manriki-gusari, sa tjat joen, kawanga and similar bladed or unbladed East Asian flail weapons, considered to have the same basic characteristics for game purposes.

items.name: Staff

availability.name: Most martial arts stores carry suitable staves; they attract much less attention than most other melee weapons

items.description: Known as jo or bo. A spear's blade makes it slash or pierce rather than bludgeon.

availability.name: Spears such as the naginata and yari typically require a bit more effort to procure than staves, but they are not widely monitored

items.name: Shortsword

availability.name: Typically must be special-ordered, although cheap versions are available in many military-supply stores (these are of dubious quality at best)

items.description: Any bladed weapon between the size of a dagger and a katana; most notably the wakizashi, typically worn paired with a katana.

items.name: Longsword

availability.name: Typically must be special-ordered, although cheap versions are available in many military-supply stores (these are of dubious quality at best)

items.description: Any blade of medium length, excluding the katana - from scimitars to Western broadswords.

items.name: Katana

availability.name: Almost certainly crafted for the individual wielding it; mass-produced katana are treated the same as longswords due to their inferior craftsmanship. Hand-crafted katana command extremely high prices and are worth every penny - they never dull, and win all ties to resist breaking or shattering

items.description: Creations of master swordsmiths, deadlier than many firearms in close combat, and especially favored by elder Kuei-jin both as weapons and status symbols. Flawed katanas are rejected by their craftsmen.

items.name: Greatsword

availability.name: Expensive but available through the same sources as other swords

items.description: Mighty blades requiring two hands to wield, such as the Japanese nodachi.
